candidates.change_summary: Change default returned AssertionPolicy to set blockAssertion true instead of false.
Change default returned AssertionPolicy to set arbitrateViaEscalationManager true instead of false.
Change default returned AssertionPolicy to set discardOracle true instead of false.
Change default returned AssertionPolicy to set validateDisputers true instead of false.
Change default returned AssertionPolicy to set multiple flags true: blockAssertion and discardOracle.
Replace the function body to always return false instead of true.
Replace the function body to return whether disputeCaller equals the zero address (true only for zero address).
Replace the function body to return whether the assertionId is non-zero (true when assertionId != 0).
Replace the function body to return the negation of the original (false when original returned true).
Replace the function body to make the result depend on both parameters: true only if disputeCaller equals the asserter encoded in assertionId (simple check using low 20 bytes).
Return a fixed nonzero price (1) instead of an empty body; function now returns int256(1).
Return a negative fixed price (-1) instead of an empty body; function now returns int256(-1).
Return the 'time' argument cast to int256 as the price (observable change depending on input).
Return the low 128 bits of the identifier (cast) as int256 to expose identifier influence on output.
Remove the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier so requestPrice can be called by anyone, changing whether PriceRequestAdded is emitted after calls (i.e., public caller control over emissions).

Add a state-changing side-effect by emitting PriceRequestAdded with msg.sender included indirectly (via ancillaryData) by prepending the caller address bytes to ancillaryData before emitting, altering observable emitted data after the call.
Invert the require to restrict the optimistic asserter differently (require msg.sender != optimisticAsserter), changing which callers can invoke requestPrice and thus whether the event is emitted.
Inserted a state-changing emit (PriceRequestAdded) call inside assertionResolvedCallback so calling it emits an event and thus changes observable behavior.
Replaced an empty body with a revert to make the function fail, changing observable state by preventing completion.

Changed the access check in onlyOptimisticAsserter to require msg.sender != optimisticAsserter, inverting the guard so authorized caller is blocked, altering observable behavior of assertionResolvedCallback.
